verdict_text:
NO

The merge is computed sequentially rather than as two task vectors against the unmodified base: `tmp = b + λ(f1-b)` and then `out = tmp + λ(f2-tmp)`, which expands to `(1-λ)²·b + λ(1-λ)·f1 + λ·f2` = `0.36·b + 0.24·f1 + 0.40·f2`, whereas the spec's formula `base + λ(ft1-base) + λ(ft2-base)` gives `0.20·b + 0.40·f1 + 0.40·f2`. This violates "Required result" clause 2, and specifically the stated arithmetic hazard in the "Why it is meaningful" section — the second task vector is taken against a base the first merge has already changed. The error is systematic across all 64 MLP tensors and far exceeds the 1e-3 relative Frobenius tolerance, so grading would fail. Everything else (name-set check, shared-tensor bit-equality check, `merged == 64`, `len(out) == 244`, float32 accumulation with cast back to the base dtype, output path) matches the specification.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
